prediction.primaryRiskSummary: Elevated moisture stress and higher nighttime temperatures reduce corn pollination success.

riskFactors.name: Mid-Season Root-Zone Moisture Deficit
riskFactors.description: SMAP observations indicate topsoil volumetric water content is 26% below historical seasonal baseline.
riskFactors.mitigationAdvice: Adopt cover crops to reduce evapotranspiration and explore supplemental drip irrigation.

riskFactors.name: Silking Heat Stress
riskFactors.description: Projected +2.4C temperature anomaly during flowering increases risk of incomplete kernel development.
riskFactors.mitigationAdvice: Shift planting window 10 days earlier or transition 30% acreage to sorghum.

recommendedCrops.recommendationReason: Sorghum requires 30-40% less water than corn and tolerates high thermal loads during vegetative and reproductive stages.
Nitrogen fixation benefits and higher regional market demand offset slight moisture risks.

prediction.recommendedIrrigationAdjustment: Introduce sensor-driven drip fertigation on high-slope zones to cut water loss by 35%.

actionPlan.title: Early Spring Planting Window Adjustment
actionPlan.action: Advance seed planting by 10 days to maximize early rainfall and avoid mid-July peak heat.
actionPlan.expectedBenefit: Shields critical silking phase from heat peaks.

actionPlan.title: Multi-Crop Diversification Pilot
actionPlan.action: Convert 15 hectares (33% of field) from corn to grain sorghum.
actionPlan.expectedBenefit: Cuts farm aggregate water requirement by 14% and reduces crop failure risk.
